turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having sharp lower chest pain and right breast pain. I also feel like I can’t breathe well and I’m sweating a lot—like I’m about to die—and I feel kind of detached from my body and surroundings.
I’m sorry you’re feeling this way. First question: **when did the chest/breast pain start, and is it constant or does it come in episodes?**

It started pretty fast—about 6 out of 10 speed, like it came on suddenly. The pain has been there with the episodes/feelings during this attack, and it’s been ongoing since it started (not really constant all day before this).
Next question: **How old are you, and do you have any history of heart or lung problems (like asthma/COPD, blood clots, or heart disease)?**
I’m 30. I don’t have heart disease or blood clots that I know of, but I do have asthma. I’ve needed a bronchodilator before.
Next question: **During this episode, do you have wheezing or a cough, or is it more like tightness/shortness of breath without wheeze?**
It’s more like tightness and shortness of breath. I don’t have a cough or wheezing that I’m noticing right now.
Next question: **Does the pain get worse with deep breaths, coughing, or moving/pressing on the chest?**

It feels worse when I breathe deeply and it’s kind of sharp with the chest area. I’m not sure about coughing because I don’t really have a cough, and I haven’t been able to tell if pressing on it changes it a lot.
Next question: **Any fever, recent infection symptoms (sore throat, runny nose, flu-like illness), or have you been sick in the last week?**
No fever and no recent infection symptoms like sore throat or runny nose. I haven’t been sick in the last week.
Next question: **Have you had any recent long travel, leg swelling/pain, or are you on estrogen/birth control or pregnant/postpartum?**
No recent long travel. I don’t have leg swelling or leg pain. I’m not pregnant/postpartum, and I’m not on estrogen or birth control that I can recall right now.
Next question: **Have you had any palpitations (feeling your heart racing/irregular), or have you ever had episodes like this?**

I do feel like my heart is racing during it, like a panic feeling, but I don’t know if it’s irregular. I’ve had anxiety episodes before, but this chest pain and breathing feeling is stronger than usual.
Next question: **Do you have any numbness/tingling, weakness, or trouble speaking, or is it mainly chest pain + shortness of breath + sweating/detached feeling?**
It’s mainly the chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, and the detached feeling. I don’t have numbness/tingling, weakness, or trouble speaking.
Next question: **Have you taken your asthma rescue inhaler during this episode—if so, did it help?**
I haven’t taken my rescue inhaler during this episode yet, so I can’t say if it would help.
Next question: **Right now, are you able to speak full sentences, and do you have any lips/face turning blue or severe worsening when lying flat?**
I can speak full sentences, but I feel really short of breath. I don’t notice my lips or face turning blue, and I haven’t noticed it getting worse when lying flat.
Next question: **Any history of blood in your sputum, recent surgery/trauma, or sudden one-sided leg symptoms (even mild)?**
No blood in sputum, no recent surgery or trauma. And no one-sided leg symptoms, even mild.
Next question: **Do you have any recent cocaine/amphetamine use, or new medications/substances (including vaping/smoking)?**
No cocaine or amphetamines. I haven’t started any new medications. I do drink alcohol heavily, but I don’t think I used anything else like vaping or smoking today.
Next question: **When you say “right breast pain,” is it localized to the skin/muscle (tender to touch) or does it feel deep inside the chest?**
It feels more like it’s in the chest area near the right breast, not like superficial skin pain. I haven’t tested it by pressing really, but it feels deep/sharp.

[ABSTAIN] I don’t yet have enough discriminating details (vital signs/oxygen level, ECG/heart rhythm, exam findings, and whether this is pleuritic vs cardiac vs asthma-related) to confidently narrow to a specific diagnosis.  
[POSSIBLE] Pulmonary embolism, Pneumonia, Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI, Acute pulmonary edema
